tools.name: pose.fromvideo
tools.description: Estimate an ordered SMPL-X pose sequence from a local video. Returns raw poses and matching FullBody constraints for downstream commands.

documentation.when_to_use: Use when a video file should be converted into a time-ordered SMPL-X pose array for downstream retargeting or analysis.
behavior: Pass an absolute video_path readable by QuickServer. Supported formats are MP4, MOV, M4V, AVI, and MKV; maximum file size is 2 GiB.
The command returns status=accepted and a request_id for continued progress tracking through generation.get.
For two people, set person to left or right to select the performer by screen position.
result_notes: A completed request returns poses in source-video order plus one top-level constraints array, fps, frame_count, source_frame_count, joint_names, betas, and rest_joints_m.

Each pose contains raw global_orient_axis_angle, body_pose_axis_angle, and translation_m values. The top-level constraints array uses the same merged raw FullBody constraint format accepted by animation generation.

Rotations are axis-angle radians; translation and rest joints are in meters. The global coordinate space is gravity-aligned Y-up. Optional incam_* fields use OpenCV camera coordinates: X-right, Y-down, Z-forward.
The result is pose data for downstream retargeting and constraint use.
scene_effects: The result is data for downstream commands and leaves Unity scene objects and animation assets unchanged.
limits: The top-level constraints array groups the sequence in the raw FullBody format for animation.generate.
The request requires QuickServer's GVHMR runtime, checkpoints, and SMPL-X Avatar asset.

video_path.description: Absolute path to a local video readable by QuickServer.

wait_seconds.description: Editor-side cooperative wait window in seconds. Values above 10 seconds are allowed; if the task is still running, return its request_id.

person.description: Select one performer by screen side in a two-person video.

tools.name: animation.generate
tools.description: Generate one animation Clip for a scene character. Use prompt for semantic motion or raw_instruction to replay an exact captured server payload; use structured constraint and trajectory fields for explicit requirements. Returns request_id and preflight diagnostics; generation.get returns the completed Clip and analysis details.

documentation.when_to_use: Submit one animation generation request for a character in the current scene context.
behavior: Describe one semantic action in prompt, or supply raw_instruction.role=generate with the exact JSON returned by generation.get(include_request_json=true).
Use structured fields for exact pose, root, effector, duration, trajectory, loop, and Clip-window requirements; see kimodo.help(section=constraints) for constraint selection.
Use point constraints and source Clip windows as documented in kimodo.help(section=constraints).
Use wait_seconds for cooperative Editor waiting; generation.get continues a running task.
result_notes: The accepted response contains request_id, status, preflight check results, and warnings. Root speed above 7 m/s warns; above 10 m/s blocks generation. Root acceleration above 10 m/s² warns; above 15 m/s blocks generation. Use the returned preflight diagnostics to assess pose/effector constraints; use pose.analysis when measured sampled joint positions are needed.

On completion, generation.get returns Clip metadata, asset path, animation_id, generation diagnostics, and post_analysis.analysis_path when analysis is enabled. Set analyze=false to omit the post-generation analysis pass.
scene_effects: A completed result is appended as a Timeline Clip; existing completed Clips are retained.
limits: Map explicit path and direction requirements to supported trajectory fields; use confirmed scene/analysis evidence to resolve details the prompt leaves unspecified. Leave other optional fields at their schema defaults.
analyze controls the full post-generation animation.analysis pass and defaults to true.
Command checks validate supported request boundaries. Evaluate semantic and artistic quality with the task's acceptance criteria and analysis evidence.

tools.name: generation.cancel
tools.description: Request cancellation of an active animation generation and return its compact lifecycle result. Use generation.get for detailed progress and diagnostics.

documentation.when_to_use: Request cancellation of an active animation generation.
behavior: Pass the exact generation request_id, then poll with generation.get to confirm its terminal state.
result_notes: Returns the compact cancellation/lifecycle result and any completed Clip metadata.
scene_effects: May stop active generation work; completed Clips remain available.
limits: Use generation.get for installation task status.
Read the returned status to confirm the cancellation state.

request_id.description: Generation request id returned by animation.generate.

outputSchema.description: Command responses keep domain fields at the top level. Success uses ok=true; command errors use ok=false and an error object. Async job failures are reported by status with an error object.

error.description: Optional command error. Command errors use {code, message, details?}; asynchronous job failures include this object while the poll command itself succeeds.

examples.description: Cancel using the exact active generation request_id.

tools.name: session.clear
tools.description: Clear the active scene context objects. The Timeline, Session data, and animation assets remain available; the next command creates a fresh scene context when needed.

documentation.when_to_use: Clear transient Kimodo context objects from the active scene Session.
behavior: Use when the current transient Session context must be reset.
result_notes: Returns whether the context was cleared, how many context objects were destroyed, and lazy recreation information.
scene_effects: Destroys scene-bound context GameObjects; persisted Timeline, History, and animation assets are retained.
limits: Call session.context after clearing to obtain fresh scene references.

examples.description: Clear the current runtime session while retaining persisted assets.

tools.name: session.history
tools.description: Read append-only command history for the active Session, a specified Session, or the global Session directory.

documentation.when_to_use: Read append-only animation command history for the current Session, a specified Session, or the global Session directory.
behavior: Omit session_id to use or create the current Session; set scope='global' to list all created Sessions.
historybegin and historyend are an inclusive operation-sequence range and must be provided together.
result_notes: Without a range, returns the 20 newest operations. Operations include the original command input and response; asynchronous generation aggregates accepted and terminal events.
scene_effects: Reads the Session's append-only history.jsonl and checks history-format and package MAJOR.MINOR compatibility.
limits: Global scope lists Sessions even when they have no operations. Patch-level package version differences within one MAJOR.MINOR are compatible.

session_id.description: Read one Session by its Timeline asset GUID; omitted uses the current Session.

scope.description: Defaults to session; set global to list all created Sessions, including Sessions with no operations.
